title: Make training fun again
summary: NH argues that training has to be fun to stay consistent, and gives three ways to make it so: pick only lifts you enjoy, schedule for excitement (including shorter sessions and putting disliked work before the fun lifts), and add a small side project as the cherry on top. His metaphor: a program is a cake you have to eat over and over.
claims: Scheduled rest days are not skipped days; missing a scheduled training day means you were under-recovered from poor programming or your training is not fun
He never feels motivated, but he loves training; motivation is too unreliable to carry you
Lifting is a hobby you chose, so there is no reason for it not to be fun
Every lift can be replaced, including squat, bench and deadlift (for example with dips, lunges and good mornings); choose lifts by their purpose and only do ones you enjoy
You don't have to squat to call yourself a lifter; that belief comes from powerlifting-centric YouTube fitness
The journey has to be enjoyable, because once you reach a goal you will want more, so the path is what really matters
Schedule for excitement: a good program can still burn you out if it is too greedy, so use smaller days or add rest days
Someone who trains like a madman for six months makes less progress than someone who trains fairly hard for two years
The most optimal program is the one you actually do; check each day is realistic, doable and exciting before tuning other variables
If you are done an hour into a 90-minute session, the last 30 minutes pay little; cut the day short or move that work to another day
People put disliked work (neck, calves) at the end and then skip it; do it before the strength work instead, and performance won't suffer
Add a small side project for fun, about 1% of total work, such as his finger push-ups, which do little for hypertrophy
You can't be a really good bodybuilder and a really good boxer at once; pick one main pursuit and keep side projects small
Lifters who just grind through training they hate don't last long
exercises: his fun side project; little hypertrophy value
